newsitem.title: UK: Airbus sees USAir deliveries starting 1998.
newsitem.headline: Airbus sees USAir deliveries starting 1998.

text.p: The European aircraft manufacturing consortium Airbus Industrie expects to start delivering aircraft under USAir Group's new order for A320 series shorthaul aircraft in 1998, industry sources said.
The sources told Reuters that under the order which was announced earlier today USAir was due to take deliveries of the initial 120 aircraft over four years starting in 1998.

The sources said it was believed that USAir still has to decide what engines it wants for the twinjets. The choice is between CFM International's CFM 56 and the International Aero Engines (IAE) consortium's V2500 engines.
CFM International is a joint venture between U.S. firm General Electric and France's Snecma.
IAE includes United Technologies Corp unit Pratt & Whitney, Britain's Rolls-Royce Plc, Daimler-Benz unit MTU and the Japanese Aero Engines Corp.
